 Toto Wolff Explains How the Cost Cap Turned Mercedes Into a Billion-Dollar Cash Cow
 Oct 17, 2025; Austin, TX, USA; Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff arrives at the track before practice for the US Grand Prix at Circuit of The Americas Austin. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images 
 By: 
 Rahaan Mazumder 
 Published: 
 October 25, 2026 - 12:00 pm 
 Rahaan Mazumder 
 October 25, 2026 
 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source 
 For the vast majority of motorsport history, owning a Formula 1 team was the absolute fastest way to completely incinerate a billionaire’s fortune. Teams essentially operated as bottomless money pits, relying on massive corporate bailouts and wealthy pay-drivers just to keep the lights on and the wind tunnels spinning.
 But if you look at the modern Formula 1 grid, the days of begging for survival are officially over. Thanks to the explosive global growth of the sport and the strict financial regulations introduced by the FIA, top F1 teams are literally printing money.
 Mercedes F1 Team Principal and co-owner Toto Wolff recently sat down for a rare, highly candid business interview on the Cheeky Pint podcast, and he pulled back the curtain on exactly how lucrative the F1 paddock has become.
 The End of the Money Pit
 Before the FIA instituted the cost cap in 2021—which strictly limits performance-related spending to a baseline of roughly $135 million—the biggest teams were locked in an infinite spending war.
 Oct 20, 2024; Austin, Texas, USA; Torger Christian Toto Wolff Team Principal and CEO of Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 walks through the track entrance before the 2024 Formula One US Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images 
 “Before we were all losing, it was a marketing exercise, but today few of us are generating very healthy profits,” Wolff explained to the podcast hosts. “You know, in our business, more than 30% EBIT margin, we are distributing dividends”.
 Because teams are no longer legally allowed to dump half a billion dollars a year into aerodynamic R&D to chase a single tenth of a second, that explosive sponsor revenue is finally turning into actual profit.
 Mercedes’ A “Billion-Dollar” Machine
 Just how big are those profits? Wolff casually dropped some staggering figures that would make Wall Street executives blush.
 “We’re generating around a billion dollars in revenue and 30% profit margin… 300 million of EBIT,” Wolff revealed.
 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Friday KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 02: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 leads George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 02, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images) 
 While a billion dollars sounds like a wildly inflated hyperbole, external financial audits actually back up Wolff’s massive flex. Recent corporate filings at the UK’s Companies House for the 2025 fiscal year revealed that the Mercedes squad pulled in over £633 million in revenue and successfully paid out a massive £125 million in dividends to its ownership trio (Wolff, INEOS, and Mercedes-Benz).
 The Ultimate Trophy Asset
 Because the grid is now locked at 11 teams—much to the absolute frustration of Michael Andretti—the sheer scarcity of an F1 entry has completely skyrocketed franchise valuations. Wolff, who holds a 33% stake in the Brackley squad, knows exactly what his empire is worth.
 “So when you invest in a Formula 1 team today, you can attribute multiples to your investment decisions,” Wolff stated, referencing a recent transaction that valued the team north of $4.6 billion. “And you know when I sold part of the team last year those multiples justified the valuation… today I’ll probably be able to generate 30% more”.
 With massive tech sponsors like CrowdStrike and Meta pouring millions into the sport and teams running highly disciplined budgets, Formula 1 has officially transformed from a playground for wealthy daredevils into one of the most ruthless, highly profitable sports leagues on the planet.
